concepts.name: Evolution and Nationalization of SBI: From Imperial Bank to SBI
key_dimensions: Imperial Bank of India (1921) formed by merger of three Presidency Banks (Bank of Bengal, Bank of Bombay, Bank of Madras)
State Bank of India Act, 1955 — nationalization and renaming; RBI held majority stake initially
Distinction from 1969/1980 nationalization waves — SBI preceded both and had a different legislative framework
SBI as an 'associated bank' consolidation: merger of 5 associate banks + Bharatiya Mahila Bank in 2017

concepts.name: SBI's Legal and Ownership Structure
key_dimensions: Governed by State Bank of India Act, 1955 — NOT the Banking Companies Act / Banking Regulation Act directly in the same manner as private banks
Government of India holds majority stake (>50%); RBI divested its stake to GoI in 2007 under SBI (Amendment) Act
SBI is a 'statutory corporation,' not a 'company' under Companies Act — implications for CAG audit, RTI applicability
Distinction: SBI Act 1955 vs. State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 — UPSC trap on which act governs what

concepts.name: SBI's Role as a Scheduled Commercial Bank vs. Its Unique Public Sector Status
key_dimensions: SBI classified as a Public Sector Bank (PSB) but governed by separate legislation unlike other PSBs (governed by Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970/1980)
SBI included in Second Schedule of RBI Act, 1934 — definition and privileges of a scheduled bank
Obligations of scheduled bank status: maintain CRR with RBI, eligible for refinance facilities
UPSC trap: SBI ≠ nationalized bank in the strict legislative sense; it was 'constituted' not 'nationalized' under 1955 Act

concepts.name: SBI as the Banker to the Government
key_dimensions: SBI acts as banker and agent to RBI under Section 45 of RBI Act for managing government accounts where RBI has no office
Distinction: RBI is the 'Banker to the Government'; SBI acts as RBI's agent — a frequently tested hierarchy
Management of Central and State government accounts, treasury operations, payment of salaries/pensions
Conflict of interest concerns: simultaneous role as commercial lender and government banker

concepts.name: SBI and Monetary Policy Transmission
key_dimensions: Role in transmitting RBI's repo rate changes to lending rates (MCLR, EBLR mechanisms)
SBI's size means its rate decisions set the benchmark for entire banking sector — 'too big to ignore' phenomenon
Stickiness of deposit rates vs. lending rates — asymmetric transmission issue
SBI's role in External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) system introduced October 2019 for retail/MSME loans

concepts.name: SBI's Capital Adequacy and Basel Norms Compliance
key_dimensions: Basel III framework implementation in India via RBI guidelines — SBI's compliance obligations
Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) requirement: minimum 9% in India vs. 8% under Basel III
SBI designated as a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB) — additional capital surcharge implications
Government recapitalization of SBI: through recap bonds, budgetary provisions — fiscal implications

concepts.name: SBI as a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB)
key_dimensions: RBI's D-SIB framework (2014) — methodology: size, interconnectedness, substitutability, complexity
SBI placed in highest bucket (Bucket 4) among D-SIBs — highest additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) surcharge (0.60%)
Other D-SIBs: ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank — SBI is the only public sector bank in the list
Global SIFI (G-SIFI) vs. D-SIB distinction — SBI not on FSB's G-SIB list (UPSC trap)

concepts.name: SBI's Non-Performing Assets (NPA) Problem and Resolution Mechanisms
key_dimensions: SBI holds largest absolute NPA volume among Indian banks — sectoral concentration in infrastructure, power, steel
Asset Quality Review (AQR) 2015 by RBI and its impact on SBI's NPA recognition
Resolution mechanisms: IBC (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code) 2016, SARFAESI Act, Debt Recovery Tribunals — SBI as largest user
SBI's internal mechanisms: Stressed Assets Management Group (SAMG), Joint Lenders' Forum (JLF) — SBI often as lead bank

concepts.name: SBI's Associate Banks and Subsidiary Structure
key_dimensions: Historical associate banks under State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 — e.g., State Bank of Patiala, State Bank of Mysore
2017 mega-merger: SBI merged 5 associate banks (SB Patiala, SB Bikaner & Jaipur, SB Mysore, SB Travancore, SB Hyderabad) + Bharatiya Mahila Bank
Rationale: economies of scale, reducing competition among PSBs, improving global ranking
Post-merger SBI became India's largest bank and ranked among top 50 globally — implications for D-SIB classification and capital requirements

concepts.name: SBI and Financial Inclusion Mandate
key_dimensions: Lead Bank Scheme — SBI assigned lead bank responsibility in specific districts; coordinates credit planning
Priority Sector Lending (PSL) obligations: 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) — SBI's compliance and shortfall to RIDF
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY): SBI as nodal bank for account opening, RuPay card issuance
Business Correspondent (BC) model — SBI's extensive BC network as last-mile delivery mechanism

concepts.name: SBI's Governance Structure and Accountability Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Central Board of Directors composition under SBI Act: Chairman (appointed by GoI in consultation with RBI), Managing Directors, Government nominated directors
Distinction from RBI's governance: SBI Chairman ≠ Governor; appointment processes differ
Parliamentary oversight: SBI's accounts audited by CAG (as it is a government company by ownership threshold) — but governed by SBI Act, not Companies Act trap
Banks Board Bureau (BBB) — now Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB): role in recommending appointments to SBI's top positions

concepts.name: SBI and Foreign Exchange / International Banking Operations
key_dimensions: SBI as an Authorised Dealer (Category I) under FEMA — can deal in all foreign exchange transactions
SBI's overseas branches and subsidiaries — role in facilitating remittances, trade finance, external commercial borrowings
SBI's role in managing India's foreign exchange reserves alongside RBI — agent bank for specific interventions
SBI's participation in NOSTRO and VOSTRO accounts — facilitating international trade settlements including Rupee trade

concepts.name: SBI's Role in Government Securities Market and Public Debt Management
key_dimensions: SBI as Primary Dealer (PD) — underwrites and makes markets in Government Securities (G-Secs)
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR): SBI's mandated holding of G-Secs, SDLs, and other approved securities
SBI's role in Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) scheme — as receiving office for subscription
When Public Debt Management Agency (PDMA) is set up, SBI's current role as primary dealer may be affected — reform debate

concepts.name: SBI's Digital Banking Initiatives and Payments Infrastructure
key_dimensions: YONO (You Only Need One) platform — integrated digital banking and lifestyle platform; SBI's response to fintech competition
SBI's role in UPI ecosystem through BHIM SBI Pay — share of UPI transactions vs. private sector banks
SBI as a member of National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) — distinction: NPCI is promoted by RBI and IBA, not owned by SBI
SBI Cards and Payment Services (SBI Card) — listed subsidiary; credit card market share and its separation from core banking

concepts.name: SBI and the Lead Bank Scheme
key_dimensions: Lead Bank Scheme introduced in 1969 on recommendations of Gadgil Study Group and Narasimham Working Group
Each district assigned to a specific bank (SBI, nationalized banks, or major private banks) as 'Lead Bank'
State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) — SBI is convener in multiple states; District Consultative Committees (DCC)
Annual Credit Plan (ACP) preparation under Lead Bank Scheme — SBI's role in coordinating district-level credit flow

concepts.name: SBI vs. RBI: Distinction in Roles, Functions, and Hierarchy
key_dimensions: RBI = central bank (monetary authority, regulator, lender of last resort); SBI = commercial bank (largest PSB)
RBI was SBI's majority shareholder until 2007; post-2007, GoI holds majority — frequently tested ownership transition
SBI borrows from RBI (repo, MSF) whereas RBI does not operate for profit — functional hierarchy in monetary transmission
Both maintain CRR but differently: RBI holds CRR deposits of all banks; SBI itself must maintain CRR with RBI

concepts.name: SBI's Role in Agricultural and Rural Credit
key_dimensions: SBI's share in Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme — largest issuer among scheduled commercial banks
Priority Sector Lending sub-targets: Agriculture (18% of ANBC), Small and Marginal Farmers (8%) — SBI's compliance
SBI vs. NABARD: SBI lends directly to farmers; NABARD refinances cooperative banks and RRBs — distinct roles often confused in UPSC
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) sponsored by SBI — e.g., Kaveri Grameena Bank; SBI holds 35% in sponsored RRBs (GoI 50%, State 15%)

concepts.name: SBI's Profit, Loss, and Financial Performance Indicators
key_dimensions: Net Interest Margin (NIM), Return on Assets (RoA), Return on Equity (RoE) — key metrics UPSC uses in data interpretation
Provisioning Coverage Ratio (PCR) — SBI's PCR as indicator of NPA management health
SBI's dividend payment to GoI — part of government's non-tax revenue; fiscal implications of SBI's profitability
Credit-to-Deposit (CD) ratio of SBI vs. industry average — implications for liquidity management and monetary transmission

concepts.name: SBI and Consolidation in the Indian Banking Sector
key_dimensions: Narasimham Committee recommendations (1991, 1998) on bank consolidation — 3-tier structure: 3 large international banks, 8-10 national banks, local banks
SBI's 2017 merger as the first major consolidation step; subsequent PSB mergers (2019-20) reduced PSBs from 27 to 12
Arguments for consolidation: scale economies, global competitiveness, reduced government recapitalization burden
Arguments against: regional representation loss, cultural integration challenges, concentration risk and D-SIB implications

concepts.name: SBI's Relationship with SEBI, Insurance Regulators, and Conglomerate Structure
key_dimensions: SBI Life Insurance (listed subsidiary) — regulated by IRDAI, not RBI; SBI holds ~55% stake
SBI Mutual Fund (SBI Funds Management) — regulated by SEBI; largest AMC by AUM
SBI Capital Markets — investment banking arm; role in PSU disinvestment, IPO management
Financial conglomerate supervision: RBI as consolidated supervisor for SBI group; inter-regulatory coordination with SEBI and IRDAI under FSDC framework
